extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, grant applicants, administrators, and institutional research offices)
extracted.subtask_description: A news/index page summarizing recent NIH extramural policy updates, resources, and guidance relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selecting appropriate research models
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches to advance understanding of human health and disease and encourages approaches that enhance human relevance and translational potential, but choice of model must be driven by the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: Understand PF5 application format and award structure
rubrics_metrics.description: Learn key features and application format for NIH’s Collaborative International Research Projects (PF5), including how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Watch NIH’s 6-minute overview to understand the new PF5 award structure and how linked awards can be created post-review; use this to prepare application format and anticipate administrative splitting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use the 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan format
rubrics_metrics.description: Prepare Data Management and Sharing Plans using the issued 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format based on a simplified set of required elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH issued a new pilot format for 2026 intended to simplify required elements—applicants should adopt this format when preparing DMS Plans to meet current expectations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed replication and reproducibility in research
rubrics_metrics.description: Incorporate replication and reproducibility practices throughout NIH-funded research to strengthen reliability and public trust.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH’s Gold Standard Science plan and the new Replication and Reproducibility Initiative encourage, drive, incentivize, and institutionalize replication and reproducibility efforts across the biomedical research enterprise; applications, awards, and program plans should reflect these priorities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpretation of 'Competitive But Not Discussed' review outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that applications in the middle third of a study section may be designated as 'competitive but not discussed'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Due to emergency modifications following resumption of activities after a lapse in appropriations, NIH designated the middle third of applications as 'competitive but not discussed' acknowledging that strong applications can fall below a 33% cut off; applicants receiving this designation should understand its implications for funding consideration and follow-up.

rubrics_metrics.name: Be aware of peer review centralization effects
rubrics_metrics.description: Understand that NIH centralized peer review within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR) to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Centralization may change review workflows and outcomes; applicants should monitor updates about consolidation and its effects on peer review processes to adapt application strategies and timing.
